title: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen / Dolo / Crocin) — CDSCO & WHO Monograph
source: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines & CDSCO Formulary
content:
Medicine: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) — 500mg, 650mg tablets / oral suspension.
Therapeutic Class: Analgesic and Antipyretic (Non-opioid, non-NSAID).
Mechanism of Action: Central inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis (COX-2 variant) within the CNS and peripheral block of pain impulse generation; acts on hypothalamic heat-regulating center.
Indications: Mild to moderate pain (headache, toothache, muscle ache, dysmenorrhea) and fever reduction.
Dosage Guidelines: Adults: 500mg to 650mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum daily dose: 4000mg (4g) per 24 hours. Children: 10-15 mg/kg per dose every 4-6 hours (Max 60 mg/kg/day).
Contraindications & Toxicities: Severe hepatic impairment, chronic alcoholism. Overdose causes acute liver necrosis via toxic metabolite NAPQI (treated with N-acetylcysteine antidote).
Brand Names: Dolo 650, Crocin, Calpol, Tylenol, Panadol.
